candidates.detail: For an active session with live presence and a valid catalog and action ID, choose_dialogue_topic looks up the shared session/action receipt and immediately returns Ok if any receipt exists, before comparing the requested topic, action kind, expected session revision or stored session catalog revision. Thus reuse of the ID from an earlier answer, join, or different topic can report success without executing the requested topic. The web topic route forwards the caller-provided action ID and, if the subsequent view succeeds, returns that view. For an answer, a matching prompt-scoped receipt returns Ok before the supplied choices are parsed or compared with the original DialogueAnswer; a different prompt or action kind is rejected. This does not imply duplicate effects or prove any normal user observed a failure. No request, database operation or browser was run.
candidates.safeguards: Both paths require the strategic gateway, accepted catalog digest and valid action ID; the topic path requires active session membership and live presence, and the answer path also checks the respondent role. Fresh answer requests validate choices and store the original actor and ballot. The normal browser source creates a fresh random action ID for each topic or answer attempt rather than deliberately replaying its prior ID, while another errantry action uses a retained retry ID. Existing committed receipts prevent repeat effect dispatch; source alone does not establish supported changed-payload retry or normal-client collision.
candidates.connected_scope: The shared DialogueAction receipt across join, topic and answer, DialogueAnswer actor and normalized ballot, session membership and catalog/revision checks, web request-to-session binding, browser request-ID lifecycle, prompt policy including multi/unanimous ordering, lost-response handling and all other producers/consumers.
